passage: Note to myself, Sunday night, after Sunaina Masi's visit. Masi had knitted Yamini a mustard-yellow sweater with a crooked green duck on the front. Yamini, who is nine and only wears blue, held it up for a long second. Then she hugged Masi and said, "I love it, it's so soft." Masi's whole face lit up. Later, in her room, Yamini asked me quietly, "Amma, was that a lie? I don't love it. But her face was so happy." I told her she had been kind, and that next time she could also find something true to say, like thanking Masi for all the hours of knitting. She wore it to the gate when Masi left.

qa.a: A crooked green duck was knitted on the front of the mustard-yellow sweater.

Dear Diary, Thursday.
Nazia aunty from next door brought a steel box of her new vegetable stew today. She watched me take the first spoon. It tasted like warm water with carrots in it. I said, "Mmm, aunty, super tasty!" She pinched my cheek and said, "Good girl, I'll make it again on Sunday, just for you."
JUST FOR ME. Now there will be more boxes.
I didn't want her to feel bad. She lives alone, and she was so excited, standing at our door in her apron. Mummy says being kind is good but I shouldn't say things I don't mean. I think next time I will say, "Thank you for thinking of me, aunty," because that part is true.
Indu

Rukmini (Class 11) has told me "All good, ma'am" four times this week, each time with a bright smile and her eyes on the floor. Tonight her roommate Kiran showed me a dance video she had made for annual day and asked Rukmini's opinion. Rukmini said, "Perfect, don't change anything."

First Sunday. Shalini planned a sunrise trek for their college group. Lavanya hates early mornings and steep paths. "Sounds amazing, count me in," she typed.
Ten days later. Lavanya gave her seminar talk, and Shalini said, "That was so good." Lavanya smiled and thanked her, but one thought kept coming back on the walk to the hostel: how would I even know? I say "so good" about everything. Maybe everyone does. She couldn't think of one person whose praise she was sure of.
The next Saturday, sitting on a rock halfway up the hill, sweaty and cold, she finally said it. "Shalini, honestly, I don't like treks. I kept saying yes." Shalini burst out laughing. "I only planned it because you said it sounded amazing!" They walked down together and found a tea stall instead.

qa.a: Her father had already handed out sweets at his shop, so she felt ashamed and afraid of disappointing him in front of everyone.

qa.q: What went wrong, and what could have helped earlier?
qa.a: Each lie needed another until the result sheet exposed it; telling her parents after the first semester, perhaps with a college counsellor's support, would have kept it fixable.

qa.q: How might Minakshi's mother have felt when she asked, "Why didn't you trust us?"
qa.a: She likely felt hurt and sad that her daughter couldn't tell her the truth, more than angry about the failed papers.

grounding: A young woman tells how hiding failed papers from a proud family turned into a trap that grew worse than the failure itself.
